exposure: Specific mutations of the HBV genome
outcome: Detection of HBV DNA in the placenta
Detection of HBV DNA in the fetus
Detection of HBV DNA in maternal blood
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 145 HBsAg-positive pregnant Thai women from whom stored samples of maternal blood, placental tissue, and cord blood were analyzed.
finding: Approximately 25% of HBV-positive mothers had fetal HBV DNA detection, often concomitant with placental detection, and HBV genotype B showed a trend towards increased risk of placental HBV DNA detection compared to genotype C.
cross-section timing: Samples collected during pregnancy/delivery (maternal blood, placental tissue, and cord blood).
